Summary: Jealous officials trapped the blameless Daniel with a law forbidding prayer to anyone but King Darius, and Daniel prayed openly anyway, as was his custom. Thrown into a den of lions, he was found unharmed at dawn — God had sent His angel and shut the lions' mouths — and Darius decreed that all should revere Daniel's God.
Significance: Decades of quiet faithfulness prepared Daniel for one public night of testing. His story anchors hope that God honours open, steady devotion — in Babylon, and in any culture that pressures believers to hide it.
